tools.name: fetch
tools.description: Fetch the full machine-readable record (JSON-LD) for one object by identifier. Accepts sat-ids (sat:section:…, sat:pier:…, sat:vessel:…, sat:poi:…, sat:trail:…, sat:report:…), section slugs, legacy OSM ids (osm:node:…), Wikidata QIDs (wikidata:Q…), GTFS stop ids (gtfs:…) and Swedish AED-registry ids

tools.name: show_section_map
tools.description: Show an interactive map of one trail section (stage) of the Stockholm Archipelago Trail, with the hiking route and ferry piers. Use this when the user wants to SEE a section on a map. Takes the same identifiers as fetch (sat:section:…, slug or uid). Pass targetKm (and optionally date) to draw a shor

tools.name: day_trip
tools.description: Plan a ready round-trip day trip to one trail section (island) of the Stockholm Archipelago Trail on a given date. Returns the best ferry hub to depart from, outbound and return ferry times, the walking time around the island and how many ferries run that day. Use this when the user wants a day-trip

tools.name: check_day_trip
tools.description: Same data as day_trip but renders NO card. Use this when you need to check or compare day trips across dates, departure hubs or stages before recommending one, or for follow-up questions where no new card is wanted. tools.name: plan_route
tools.description: Plan a multimodal A→B route between two trail sections (islands), or between an island and a mainland ferry hub (Strömkajen, Vaxholm, Årsta, Stavsnäs …): walk → ferry → walk, with departure/arrival times, walking distances and pier names. tools.name: multi_day
tools.description: Plan a multi-day trip on the Stockholm Archipelago Trail: an overnight stay on one island, or an island hop across up to four stages, with the ferries and the walk for each day. Use this when the user wants a hike over several days, an overnight stay on an island, or to combine two or more islands.

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "search" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: Search the published objects of the Stockholm Archipelago Trail: trail sections (stages), the trail itself, ferry piers, ferry vessels, reviewed public reports …

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "search" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "fetch" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Description uses pressure/override language
findings.detail: Description of "show_section_map" stacks urgency/override words (important, never). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.
